name: Extreme heat
summary: Heatwave warnings in parts of Queensland and southern Africa; no top-tier warnings over large populations
state: The Bureau of Meteorology has heatwave warnings in force for parts of Queensland, centred on the Gulf Country, which is sparsely populated (BoM; ABC News, 2 Nov). Zimbabwe and central Mozambique have also issued heat warnings as El Niño brings a hotter, drier summer. As of 6 Nov no deadly heatwave or top-tier warning covering a large population was found, so the level stays Normal, but the risk is rising across the Southern Hemisphere.
for_you: In Australia, follow Bureau of Meteorology heatwave warnings and state health advice. Older people, young children and outdoor workers are most exposed when heat builds early in the season.
rubric_hit: No major heatwave with top-tier warnings over a large population; regional warnings only (Normal)

why: Heat is the deadliest weather hazard globally, straining power grids, crops and health systems.
drivers: Heat domes, climate warming, season, humidity, urban heat islands.

rubric.alert: Deadly heatwave with top-tier official warnings across a large population.
rubric.watch: Heatwave warnings across a major region, or national temperature records.
rubric.normal: No major heatwaves affecting large populations.
